Topic: Introduction - What is the Internet
- The Internet is just a huge network of wires (incl. undersea fiber-optic cables) connecting computers worldwide.
- Server = always-on computer that serves data/files on request. Client = the device requesting them.
- ISP (Internet Service Provider) relays your request to a DNS server.
- DNS server = phone book that translates a domain name (google.com) into an IP address.
- IP address = unique numeric "postal code" for every device on the Internet.
- Flow: Browser -> ISP -> DNS (resolves IP) -> Browser requests directly from that IP -> server responds with page data.

Topic: Introduction - How Do Websites Actually Work
- Server sends back 3 file types: HTML (content), CSS (styling), JavaScript (functionality).
- House analogy: HTML = bricks, CSS = paint/decor, JS = electricity/appliances.
- Browser render order: HTML first (raw content) -> CSS applied (styled) -> JS runs (interactive).
- Chrome DevTools (right-click -> Inspect) lets you view/edit the live HTML locally; edits are lost on refresh since the browser re-fetches the real files from the server.

Topic: HTML - Elements (Headings, Paragraphs, Void Elements, Lists, Nesting, Anchors, Images)
- Tag = the <bracketed> bit; Element = opening tag + content + closing tag together.
- Headings h1-h6 show hierarchy (like a book TOC); convention: only one h1, don't skip levels.
- Paragraph <p> separates text blocks and lets screen readers navigate paragraph-by-paragraph.
- Void elements (<hr />, <br />, <img />) self-close, no separate closing tag; don't use <br /> as a substitute for a new <p> (breaks accessibility).
- Lists: <ul> = bullets (order doesn't matter), <ol> = numbered (order matters); both need <li> children; <ol start="n"> changes starting number.
- Nesting: a sub-list goes inside its parent <li>, before that <li>'s closing tag; indentation is for humans, not the browser, but VS Code auto-indent doubles as a bug-finder.
- Attributes live in the opening tag (name="value"); href is anchor-specific, draggable is a global attribute usable on any element.
- <img src="..." alt="...">: alt text is read by screen readers - always add it for meaningful images.
- Practiced across EX 2.1-3.4, capped by EX 3.4 Birthday Invite Project combining headings + image + list + link.

Topic: Multi Page websites - File Paths, Web Pages, Boilerplate, Portfolio & Hosting
- File path = unique location of a file/folder; root = the hard drive (C:\ on Windows, Macintosh HD on Mac).
- Absolute path = from the root (C:\Project\Images\cat.png); works anywhere but breaks if the project moves.
- Relative path = from the file you're writing in; USE THIS in web dev (shorter + survives moving the project).
- Special chars: ./ = current directory (always write it for same-folder files), ../ = go up one level (chain ../../ for more).
- Multi-page site = several .html files linked with <a href="./public/about.html">; keep index.html at top level, other pages in public/, assets in assets/images/.
- href is for <a> (links); src is for <img> (resources) - never swap them. An <img> can be nested inside an <a> to make an image a link.
- HTML boilerplate: <!DOCTYPE html> (HTML5) -> <html lang="en"> (root) -> <head> (invisible info: meta charset UTF-8, viewport, title=tab text) + <body> (all visible content). VS Code: type ! + Enter to auto-generate (only in .html files).
- Portfolio project (EX 4.3): 7-step build (boilerplate -> title -> move projects to public/ -> screenshots -> titles -> project links -> preview images + About/Contact). Use height="200" to shrink big screenshots.
- Web hosting = putting files on an always-on web server so anyone can reach them 24/7 (vs local development = files only on your machine).
- GitHub Pages deploy: public repo + README -> Upload files (drag folder CONTENTS, not the folder) -> Commit -> Settings > Pages > Branch = main -> Save -> wait 1-10 min for live URL. Home page MUST be named exactly index.html (lowercase i).

Topic: CSS - Styling, Selectors, Cascade, Box Model, Layout & Projects
- CSS = Cascading Style Sheets = the styling layer (paint/decor); "cascades" from general to specific. Separation of concerns from HTML content.
- Every rule = property: value; (e.g. color: blue;). Internal/external rules also need a selector + { }.
- 3 ways to add CSS: inline (style="..." attr, one element), internal (<style> in <head>, one page), external (.css file via <link rel="stylesheet" href="./style.css">, multi-page - most common).
- Selectors: element (tag), .class (reusable), #id (unique, one per page), [attr] / [attr="val"], * (universal/all). Same syntax as Selenium/Cypress CSS locators.
- Combining: A, B = group; A > B = direct child (one level); A B = descendant (any depth); AB (e.g. li.done) = chain (no spaces, element first).
- Cascade (decides conflicts): 1.Position (lower wins) -> 2.Specificity (ID > attribute > class > element) -> 3.Type (external < internal < inline) -> 4.Importance (!important beats all). Some props (font-family) inherit.
- Colors: named (cornflowerblue), hex (#5D3891), rgb(93,56,145). color=text, background-color=background. colorhunt.co for palettes.
- Fonts: font-size units px/pt (static), em (rel to parent), rem (rel to root <html> - PREFERRED). font-weight normal/bold/100-900. font-family: "Name", genericBackup; (sans-serif/serif/monospace/cursive/fantasy) - quote multi-word names. Google Fonts via <link> in <head>. text-align left/right/center/start/end.
- Box model (inside->out): content(width/height) -> padding (inside border) -> border (thickness style color; grows OUTWARD, doesn't change size) -> margin (outside). Shorthand clockwise T R B L; 2 vals = TB LR; 1 val = all. <div> = invisible grouping container. <p> has default 1em margin - zero it when needed.
- DevTools: Inspect / Ctrl+Shift+I. Styles tab (struck-out = overridden), Computed tab (final values + inherited), CSS Overview (grab a site's colors/fonts). Edits are local-only, reset on refresh.
- display: block (full width, stacks below - default), inline (same line, CAN'T set w/h), inline-block (same line + settable w/h), none (hidden). <span> is inline by default.
- position: static (default flow), relative (to its own original spot), absolute (to nearest positioned ancestor, else page top-left; leaves flow), fixed (to browser window, stays on scroll). Idiom: parent position:relative + child position:absolute. z-index = stacking (default 0, higher on top, -1 behind). border-radius:50% = circle.
- Projects: Color Vocab (link external CSS at right path, id selectors, shared class, size imgs in CSS); Flag of Laos (class-less HTML -> target with combined selectors + cascade + relative/absolute + border-radius:50%; reset <p> margins; hex via CSS Overview); Motivational Poster (5px border, black bg, Google font Libre Baskerville, simple centering via width:50% + margin-left:20% + margin-top; learn text-transform:uppercase from docs).

Topic: FLEXBOX - Display Flex & Flex Direction (EX 9.0, EX 9.1)
- Problem: old layout used hacks - <table> for styling (semantically wrong), inline-block (fiddly), position:absolute (inflexible), float (designed for wrapping text around images, not page layout). Flexbox is built for laying boxes out in a row/column.
- Turn it on with display:flex on the CONTAINER (the parent wrapping the items) - never on the children.
- Once a container is flex, children's own default display values (block/inline/list-item) are IGNORED - Flexbox takes over. Think of it as a separate system from display:block/inline/inline-block.
- Default: items sit in a horizontal row, each sized to fit its content.
- gap adds spacing between items: gap:10px (static) or gap:1rem (scales with root font size).
- display:flex = container is full width (like block). display:inline-flex = container shrinks to fit its content and other things can sit on the same line (like inline-block). Children layout is identical either way.
- flex-direction:column stacks items vertically (row is the default).
- Selecting flex items: .container div = all div descendants (any depth); .container > div = direct child divs; .container > * = ALL direct children regardless of tag (safest for "style every flex item"); .container > :is(div,p) = composable version.
- EX 9.0: turned an <li> list into a nav bar with display:flex + gap on .container (list-style:none removes bullets).
- EX 9.1: 7 coloured divs, .container display:inline-flex + flex-direction:column, .container > * { flex-basis:100px; }.
- Modern layout tools = Flexbox, Grid, Bootstrap. Keep float for its original job (text wrapping around an image).

Topic: FLEXBOX - Flex Layout (order, flex-wrap, justify-content, align-items, align-self, align-content)
- order (child prop): default 0 for every item; lower number goes first, ties break by HTML source order; purely visual - doesn't change DOM/accessibility order.
- flex-wrap (container prop): nowrap (default, no hyphen - items squeeze then overflow) vs wrap (drops to a new line) vs wrap-reverse (new lines stack bottom-to-top instead of top-to-bottom).
- justify-content (container prop, MAIN axis spacing): flex-start/flex-end/center/space-between/space-around/space-evenly - only visible once items don't already fill all the space.
- align-items (container prop, CROSS axis spacing): flex-start/flex-end/center/baseline/stretch (default); needs the container to have extra height (e.g. height:70vh) to actually see it working; baseline aligns text baselines not box edges (only differs from flex-start when items' font-size/padding differ).
- align-self (child prop): same values as align-items but overrides just one item, letting it opt out of the container's align-items.
- align-content (container prop): spaces the GAPS BETWEEN WRAPPED LINES; only has any effect with flex-wrap:wrap/wrap-reverse AND 2+ lines - easy to confuse with align-items (which positions items within one line, not the lines themselves).
- Resources: CSS-Tricks Flexbox cheat sheet (separates parent vs child properties - look up, don't memorize), Flexbox Froggy game (Intermediate difficulty) and the flex-layout demo playground.
- Next lesson: Flexbox sizing (flex-grow/flex-shrink/flex-basis).

Topic: FLEXBOX - Flex Sizing (flex-grow / flex-shrink / flex-basis)  *** WEAK AREA - REVISE EVERY TIME ***
- PRIORITY LADDER (course formula slide): Content width < width < flex-basis < min-width/max-width. Rightmost = strongest, applied last.
- The lesson phrases it as a LOOKUP: "first it looks at whether min-width/max-width is set; if not, is there a flex-basis?; if not, the width (or height on a column); if none of those, the actual content width." Walk down the list until you hit something that IS set.
- "CONTENT WIDTH" IS NOT ONE NUMBER - IT'S A RANGE: max-content = all the text on ONE line (the "ideal estate"); min-content = the single LONGEST WORD at that font-size. With no sizing props at all, an item starts at max-content and shrinks toward min-content.
- SHRINKING IS NOT UNIFORM: each item has its OWN floor because each has its own longest word. In the demo the box containing "programming" stays widest - flexbox refuses to break a word across lines.
- PAST THE FLOOR IT DOESN'T KEEP SHRINKING - it overflows: the content "gets pushed off the page and will not be visible on screen anymore".
- width and flex-basis behave IDENTICALLY under pressure - both are only a PREFERRED size, abandoned when there's no room. 4 items x width:100px + gap:10px needs ~430px; above that every item is exactly 100px, below it the 100px is dropped and each item shrinks to its own min-content. Only difference between them: who wins the lookup.
- The lesson on setting both: "there's actually not even any point in setting it [width], because it's going to be looking at the more important property" - delete the width.
- THE 3 QUESTIONS (instructor's debugging method - use before writing any CSS): drag the window edge and ask (1) Does it grow? -> flex-grow (2) Does it shrink? -> flex-shrink (3) What size does it want to be? -> flex-basis.
- flex-basis = the REQUESTED/starting size of a flex item. max-width = a HARD CEILING, min-width = a HARD FLOOR. They are not the same kind of property.
- If flex-basis is set, WIDTH IS COMPLETELY IGNORED - but only on the MAIN axis. Row container -> basis = width (height still works). Column container -> basis = HEIGHT (width still works).
- If the basis can't be honoured, the item falls back down the ladder to its MINIMUM CONTENT WIDTH and stops there.
- Order of operations: browser sizes the item first (flex-basis, then flex-grow/flex-shrink), THEN clamps it between min-width and max-width. Clamping happens last.
- Scenario 1: flex-basis:200px + max-width:100px -> basis BREAKS the ceiling, so flex-basis is overruled -> FINAL WIDTH = 100px.
- Scenario 2: flex-basis:50px + max-width:200px -> basis RESPECTS the ceiling, so max-width never kicks in -> FINAL WIDTH = 50px.
- Scenario 3: flex-basis:200px + min-width:300px -> basis BREAKS the floor, so flex-basis is overruled -> FINAL WIDTH = 300px.
- Scenario 4: flex-basis:400px + min-width:300px -> basis RESPECTS the floor, so min-width never kicks in -> FINAL WIDTH = 400px.
- Careful: swap scenario 4's min-width for max-width:300px and the answer flips to 300px. Always name the limit first - ceiling or floor?
- Say it out loud: max-width = the item's potential to EXTEND (how big it's ALLOWED to get). min-width = the item's potential to SHRINK (how small it's ALLOWED to get). Neither is a goal - they only draw the allowed range; flex-basis is the only one actually ASKING for a size.
  * flex-basis does NOT respect the limit -> the limit steps in and becomes the final width (basis>max-width -> max-width wins; basis<min-width -> min-width wins).
  * flex-basis DOES respect the limit -> the limit stays out of it and flex-basis becomes the final width (basis<max-width or basis>min-width -> basis wins).
- Shortcut: final width = clamp(min-width, size-from-flex-basis/grow/shrink, max-width) -> vs max-width the SMALLER wins, vs min-width the LARGER wins.
- Traps: (1) max-width also caps flex-grow (item grows into free space then stops dead at the ceiling); (2) min-width BEATS max-width (min-width:300px + max-width:100px -> 300px, floor is applied last).
- THE 3 LEVERS (all are CHILD properties): flex-grow "do I take a share of spare space?" (default 0 = NO) / flex-shrink "do I give up size when overflowing?" (default 1 = YES) / flex-basis "what size do I start from?" (default auto).
- grow & shrink are RATIOS, not pixels. flex-grow:5 = "give me 5 shares of the leftover while a 1-item gets 1 share".
- gs-1 flex:0 0 100px -> RIGID. Cannot grow, cannot shrink. Width is constant 100px, no flexibility.
- gs-2 flex:1 0 100px -> 100px is the FLOOR. Grows unlimited into available space, but will NOT shrink below 100px.
- gs-3 flex:0 1 100px -> 100px is the CEILING. Shrinks freely down to min-content, but will NOT grow past 100px. *** THIS IS THE DEFAULT (flex: 0 1 auto) - you are allowed to shrink, you are NOT allowed to grow. ***
- gs-4 flex:1 1 100px -> fully fluid, range = min-content to available space. The 100px never survives as a final width ("dummy piece") BUT it is still the STARTING LINE - free space is measured after every basis is laid down.
- Proof the basis is not truly ignored in gs-4: same 2 items (short word + long sentence) in 600px -> flex:1 1 auto gives 182/418, flex:1 1 0 gives 300/300.
- flex-basis:auto = CONTENT PRIORITY (10-word sentence gets max room, single word gets min room) - share the LEFTOVERS. flex-basis:0 = EQUAL WIDTH for all - share EVERYTHING.
- SHORTHAND: flex: <grow> <shrink> <basis>;  e.g. grow1/shrink1/basis0 -> flex: 1 1 0 -> shortened further to just flex: 1 (most commonly used).
- Presets: flex:1 = 1 1 0% | flex:2 = 2 1 0% | flex:auto = 1 1 auto | flex:none = 0 0 auto | flex:initial = 0 1 auto (default) | flex: 0 0 250px = hard 250px sidebar.
- CORRECTION worth remembering: flex:2 is NOT "2 2 0". One number sets flex-GROW only; shrink stays 1 and basis becomes 0%. (Verified in Chrome.) The 1:2:3 result is unaffected because with basis 0 there is nothing to shrink.
  * NOT a mis-hearing - the transcript itself says "in this case, it's a grow of 2 and a shrink of 2". That is a slip in the video (flex:1 -> grow 1/shrink 1 is right only because the DEFAULT shrink already is 1). Trust the browser: a single number never touches flex-shrink.
- COURSE EXERCISE: https://appbrewery.github.io/flexbox-sizing-exercise/ - make the blue flexbox behave like the green one. Ideal widths 200/200/400. Solution = justify-content:space-between on the container + flex-basis 200/200/400 + flex-shrink:0 on items 2 AND 3 (item 1 keeps the default shrink). Trap: the edge spacing is justify-content, not a sizing property.
- GOTCHA: the shorthand resets basis to 0, the longhand doesn't. flex-grow:1 alone -> basis stays auto (content-weighted widths). flex:1 -> basis 0% (equal widths). This explains most "why aren't my columns equal" bugs.
- RATIOS: flex:1 / flex:2 / flex:3 in a 600px row -> 100px / 200px / 300px (6 shares total). They grow AND shrink together, always keeping 1x : 2x : 3x.
- The 5-step algorithm: (1) lay down every basis (2) free space = container - sum(basis) - GAPS - margins (3) positive free space -> share by grow ratio; negative -> claw back by shrink x basis (4) clamp to min/max-width (5) justify-content positions whatever is left.
- Asymmetry: grow is a plain ratio, shrink is WEIGHTED BY BASIS. Verified: basis 200 + basis 400 squeezed into 300px -> 100px and 200px (not 50/250) - the bigger item can afford the bigger haircut.
- #1 REAL-WORLD BUG: every flex item silently has min-width:auto = its min-content size, so flex-shrink cannot cross it. Verified: a 100px box holding "Antidisestablishmentarianism" stayed 190px wide until min-width:0 was added. Fix = min-width:0 (or overflow:hidden). Causes the classic "text-overflow ellipsis doesn't work" issue.
- Other gotchas: flex-basis sizes the CONTENT BOX (use box-sizing:border-box); flex-basis:50% is a % of the CONTAINER's main size; images don't shrink politely (min-width:0 + max-width:100%); margin-left:auto shoves an item to the far end (navbar trick).
- Patterns: equal columns .row>*{flex:1} | sidebar .sidebar{flex:0 0 250px}+.content{flex:1;min-width:0} | responsive cards {flex:1 1 250px}+flex-wrap:wrap | centering justify-content:center + align-items:center.
- Full notes: .github/my_tasks/concepts/concept_flex_sizing.md | Tasks: .github/my_tasks/tasks/flex_sizing_tasks.md | Hard copy: flexbox_master_notes.pdf

Topic: FLEXBOX - EX 9.4 Pricing Table Project (section capstone, built 2026-08-23)
- Brief: 3 pricing cards. Only hard requirement = the flexbox part: cards adapt their width in a row, and STACK vertically below a breakpoint via a media query. Everything else is personal preference. Starter gave all the HTML + the Sono font + an EMPTY @media (max-width:1250px){} block as the hint.
- THE WHOLE PROJECT IS 4 IDEAS: (1) centring cheat code (2) flex:1 + max-width card (3) kill the ul bullets+indent (4) media query flex-direction:column.
- CENTRING CHEAT CODE: display:flex + justify-content:center + align-items:center + a height on the container = centred vertically AND horizontally. Genuinely hard before flexbox.
- THE CARD PATTERN TO MEMORISE: .pricing-plan { flex: 1; max-width: 400px; } -> "share the row equally and stay fluid, but never get wider than this". Fluid AND capped. The max-width clamps the grow result at the end (flex-sizing step 4).
- *** TRAP 1 - height:100vh MUST become height:100% when the cards stack. *** Measured at 760x900: with 100vh the container is locked to 804px but the stacked content needs 895px -> the first card's top edge sits at -82px, ABOVE the top of the page. With height:100% the container grows to 967px and nothing is cut.
  * WHY IT'S WORSE THAN NORMAL OVERFLOW: justify-content:center splits the overflow BOTH ways. You can scroll to the bottom half. You can NEVER scroll to the top half. The "Basic" heading was permanently unreachable.
  * The instructor demos this on purpose: "when you scroll to the top and the bottom, it actually cuts off a bunch of stuff."
  * RULE: 100vh = "exactly one screen, no more". Right for a row that fits one screen, wrong the moment content stacks. Prefer min-height:100vh (one screen MINIMUM, free to grow).
- *** TRAP 2 - padding:0 on the <li> does NOTHING. *** Both the bullet and the indent belong to the <ul>: the browser default padding-left:40px is on the ul only. Measured: li{padding:0} -> ul padding-left still 40px; .plan-features{padding:0} -> 0px. With text-align:center a ul that's 40px narrower on the left centres its text 20px too far right - that was the subtle misalignment.
  * How to catch it: DevTools -> select the <ul> -> Computed tab -> read padding-left. Don't guess which element owns a default.
- TRAP 3 - selector hygiene: the HTML already gave me .plan-features and .plan-button. Bare li{} / button{} selectors leak to every list/button on the page and throw away work already done for me.
- TRAP 4 - media query hygiene: only override what CHANGES (flex-direction + height). Re-declaring display/justify-content/align-items/gap hides the intent and gives you two places to edit gap later.
- CSS UNITS (the questions this project raised): px = absolute (borders, precise nudges) | rem = root font-size, default 16px so 1rem=16px (layout spacing, gap - scales with zoom) | em = PARENT font-size, compounds | % = parent's matching dimension | vw = 1% of viewport WIDTH | vh = 1% of viewport HEIGHT.
- AXIS DISCIPLINE: height:100vh OK / max-width:400px OK / max-width:30vw OK / max-width:50vh WRONG - a width capped by the screen HEIGHT. No syntax error warns you, it just behaves oddly as the window changes shape. (That was my submission #2.)
- 30vw is ~384px on a 1280px screen, so not "wrong" - but max-width:400px wins because a card has a READABLE width, which is a property of the text, not of the window.
- gap:2rem vs 32px: same pixels today, but rem stays proportional if the user zooms or html{font-size} changes. Spacing tied to type = design system; px = fixed guess.
- MY ITERATION LOG: #1 flex-basis:440px (rigid) -> #2 flex:1 + max-width:50vh (right idea, wrong axis) -> #3 flex:1 + max-width:400px (sizing correct) -> final: + height:100%, .plan-features reset, scoped selectors, border-radius:5px.
- PATTERN IN MY OWN MISTAKES: the layout thinking was right every time. What tripped me up was WHICH ELEMENT owns a property (ul vs li) and WHICH AXIS a unit belongs to (vh vs width). Both are "read the property, not the vibe" errors.
- Full notes: .github/my_tasks/concepts/concept_pricing_table_project.md | Tasks: .github/my_tasks/tasks/pricing_table_project_tasks.md

Topic: GRID - Display Grid (EX 10.0 Chessboard)
- Problem: Flexbox aligns along ONE line. A magazine/dashboard layout needs BOTH axes at once - doable in Flexbox only by nesting containers inside containers. Grid was built for 2D layouts.
- THE DISTINCTION: Flexbox = 1D (a row OR a column), Grid = 2D (rows AND columns together). If the design has an X and a Y, use Grid.
- NOT an either/or. Real sites nest them: a Flexbox INSIDE a grid cell (the transcript's Swiss weather site does exactly this - a flex-direction:column flexbox inside a grid panel), or a Grid inside a Flexbox. Flexbox was not wasted learning.
- BEHAVIOUR DIFFERENCE on resize: Grid snaps everything to shared row/column lines so all gaps stay dead straight. Flexbox squishes/adapts content, so items only line up by accident. Demo: https://appbrewery.github.io/grid-vs-flexbox/
- You CAN make a 1D grid, it just behaves differently to a flexbox.
- Turn it on with display:grid on the CONTAINER (same muscle memory as display:flex).
- Container props: grid-template-columns (how many cols + how wide), grid-template-rows (how many rows + how tall), gap (gutter between tracks - the SAME gap property from Flexbox, spaces both rows and columns).
- Syntax = one value per track, space separated. "1fr 2fr" = 2 columns, 2nd twice as wide. "1fr 1fr 1fr 1fr" = 4 equal columns.
- fr = FRACTION OF THE AVAILABLE SPACE. It's a RATIO, not a size. 1fr 2fr -> if col1 is 100px, col2 is 200px.
- fr is basically flex-grow with its own unit - same ratio thinking as flex:1 / flex:2 / flex:3 -> 100/200/300 in a 600px row.
- *** TRAP (my actual bug this lesson) - 1fr OF NOTHING IS NOTHING. *** grid-template-rows with 1fr + no height on the container = 0px rows = COMPLETELY BLANK PAGE, even though all 64 divs and their background-colors were there.
  * WHY the columns worked but the rows didn't: a grid container's defaults are ASYMMETRIC. "The default behavior for a grid container is to try and take up the full width, but only have as much height as it allows to fit the content." Width = block-level so it fills the parent (real space for 1fr to split). Height = shrinks to content, and empty divs have 0 content -> 0.
  * Same trap family as align-items needing a container height in Flexbox. Check the CONTAINER's height before blaming the grid.
- GRID INFERS: declare only 8 columns and drop in 64 divs and you ALREADY get the chessboard - grid auto-creates rows (items 1-8 = row 1, 9-16 = row 2...). Declaring grid-template-rows anyway is clearer + gives you control.
- repeat(n, size) = shorthand for identical tracks. repeat(8, 1fr) == 1fr x8. repeat(8, 100px) for fixed.
- GRID ITEMS STRETCH TO FILL THEIR CELL by default, on BOTH axes (same idea as align-items:stretch in Flexbox, applied twice). That's why empty unstyled divs work - size the CELL and the square fills it. Also why a background-color paints the whole cell.
- EX 10.0 CHESSBOARD: 64 pre-written .white/.black divs -> 8x8 board, 100x100px squares, #f0d9b5 / #b58863.
- TWO VALID SOLUTIONS, opposite directions:
  * (a) SIZE THE CHILDREN (official solution): .container{width:800px; display:grid; repeat(8,1fr) both} + .white,.black{width:100px;height:100px}. Columns = 800/8. Rows have no container height so they size to CONTENT - and the content is 100px tall, so rows become 100px and the container grows to 800px by itself.
  * (b) SIZE THE CONTAINER (my solution): .container{width:800px; height:800px; display:grid; repeat(8,1fr) both} + only background-colors on the squares. Both axes have 800px for 1fr to split -> 100px tracks -> items stretch to fill. No size needed on the children at all.
  * Pixel-identical output. (b) is the more idiomatic grid approach - let the GRID dictate sizes to the children instead of forcing sizes on children and letting grid infer itself. Bonus: change 800px to 640px in ONE place and the whole board resizes.
- WHY width:800px on the container at all: without it the container fills the full window, so 1fr columns get much wider than 100px. The squares stay 100px but their CELLS don't - that's the "mystery gaps between squares" effect. 8 x 100px = 800px makes cells exactly square-sized. (Instructor: not setting the width is fine, the exercise is really about display:grid + grid-template-columns.)
- GRADED 10/10. Only debugging step needed was the missing container height. Approach chosen was the more scalable of the two.
- Say it out loud: "Flexbox = one line, Grid = a table." / "fr is flex-grow with a unit." / "fr of nothing is nothing." / "Grid container is greedy sideways, shy downwards." / "You don't size chess squares, you size the board."
- Next: 10.1 Grid Sizing -> 10.2 Grid Placement -> 10.3 Mondrian Project.
- Full notes: .github/my_tasks/concepts/concept_grid_display.md | Tasks: .github/my_tasks/tasks/grid_display_tasks.md

Topic: GRID - Grid Sizing (Fixed / Auto / Fractional / MinMax / Repeat)
- Problem: EX10.0 only needed identical fr squares. Real layouts need a mix - some tracks locked, some flexible-but-capped, some that just eat leftover space - and have to survive item counts that don't match the template.
- Fixed sizing (px or rem) = NEVER responsive to window resize. rem still reacts to ROOT font-size (zoom/html{font-size}), not to browser width - relative-to-root != responsive-to-screen.
- grid-template shorthand: `rows / columns` in one line (e.g. `grid-template: 100px 200px / 400px 800px;`). Deliberately avoided while learning - explicit rows/columns props are easier to debug/spot typos in. Recognise it, don't write it yet.
- *** auto row vs auto column - THIS LESSON's trap, same family as EX10.0's blank-page trap ***: auto COLUMN = extensible, stretches/shrinks so columns always total 100% of width. auto ROW = does NOT fill height - just fits its own CONTENT height. Same "width-greedy, height-shy" asymmetry as a grid container's own defaults, just now behind an explicit keyword.
- fr = ratio of available space (same idea as EX10.0). NEW GOTCHA: fr ROWS are not independently sized - they're a live ratio. Grow the content in ONE fr row and Grid may grow a SIBLING fr row too (even though its content never changed), purely to preserve the ratio (e.g. 1fr:1fr must always match). Proven in the transcript's own demo (adding text to row 2 grows row 1).
- minmax(min, max) = one function combining Flexbox's min-width + max-width (Selva's weak area) into ONE grid-track property. Grows up to max, shrinks down to min, refuses to cross either line.
- repeat(count, value) works for ANY track size, not just fr (e.g. repeat(2, 200px)).
- Fewer items than template cells (e.g. 2x3=6 cells, only 4 items) -> Grid fills left-to-right then wraps rows; leftover cells are just EMPTY, not phantom boxes.
- More items than template cells (e.g. 2x2=4 cells, 5th item added) -> Grid auto-creates an implicit row. Default sizing: WIDTH matches existing column tracks, HEIGHT fits the new item's own content (same "shy" rule as an auto row). Override with grid-auto-rows / grid-auto-columns (e.g. grid-auto-rows:300px) - useful for dynamically-added content (JS rows, a growing game board).
- Chrome DevTools: elements with display:grid show a "grid" badge -> click to toggle the on-page overlay; Layout pane lets you change overlay colour, toggle line numbers, and (most useful) "Show track sizes" to read exact computed px values of every row/column without doing the math yourself.
- EX 10.1 Grid Sizing ("Test" page, `course_content/GRID/EX 10.1 Grid Sizing/test.html`) - not yet attempted. Spec: rows 1fr/1fr/2fr + an out-of-template 4th row at fixed 50px via grid-auto-rows; columns auto/400px/minmax(200px,500px). Instructor's own advice: pause and write the CSS yourself first. Common typo trap: dropping the "s" from grid-template-rows/-columns (fails silently).
- Say it out loud: "auto column stretches, auto row just fits." / "fr rows are a ratio, not a fixed size - grow one, and its siblings may grow too." / "minmax = Flexbox's min/max-width, merged into one grid function." / "Too few items = empty cells. Too many items = implicit rows, sized by column width + content height, unless grid-auto-rows says otherwise."
